problem: Ghost tasks keep re-appearing: _sync_runtime_to_tasks recreates closed tasks from stale events; no workflow rule to clean runtime_errors.json on task close
root_cause: _sync_runtime_to_tasks recreated closed tasks from stale events; no workflow rule to clean runtime_errors.json
solution: 1) server.py: skip re-creation if closed/resolved task exists for same key. 2) CLAUDE.md step 3.7: added runtime event cleanup command

problem: E-FILE-003: read_text_file reads entire file before truncating; file tools return E-CP-003 instead of E-FILE-NNN codes
root_cause: E-FILE-003: read_text_file called target.read_text() loading entire file before truncating; file tools raised RuntimeError giving generic E-CP-003
solution: stream-read up to budget chars; file handlers return success:False with E-FILE-NNN codes

problem: ptt.md missing E-PTT-003 watchdog; map.md missing waiting status and closed_keys ghost prevention
root_cause: ptt.md had no E-PTT-003 entry; map.md missing waiting status and ghost task prevention docs
solution: ptt.md: added E-PTT-003 row. map.md: waiting in 3 places, ghost prevention, cleanup rule.

problem: Add split-view to Flow tab: current steps left, ideal doc right
root_cause: Flow tab had no way to view ideal planned state alongside current steps
solution: Added /flow-ideal/<id> endpoint in server.py, split-view CSS, and DOM-based markdown renderer in map.html

problem: Update ideal/system.md — full lifecycle: startup sequence, first-run branch, versioned tutorial, watchdog, shutdown
root_cause: system.md had only 8 steps, missing startup sequence, post-startup branching, versioned tutorial, and MCP/Storage details
solution: Rewrote Processing Pipeline into 4 blocks: startup, post-startup branching, request loop, watchdog+shutdown. Added TUTORIAL_VERSION concept, full error map, storage table.

problem: Detail Block 3 in system.md + config.yaml: add audio pipeline steps, link PTT as sub-flow of System
root_cause: system.md Block 3 had no audio pipeline detail; config.yaml system flow had 7 steps without PTT drill-down link
solution: Updated system.md Block 3 with 11 steps (mic→gRPC→Whisper→LLM→TTS→SLEEPING); config.yaml system flow updated to 11 steps; PTT flow gets parent:system for drill-down

problem: Expand Block 3 in system.md + config.yaml: add audio_ducking, separate grpc_transport/speech_recognition, add memory read/write steps
root_cause: Block 3 had 6 merged steps missing audio_ducking, separate transport/recognition, memory read+write
solution: Expanded to 16 steps across 5 sections: capture, transmission, recognition, LLM, audio response, completion

problem: Update PTT flow: detailed steps with correct modules for drill-down, add architecture diagrams to ideal/ptt.md
root_cause: PTT steps used grpc_service x3 for everything; no architecture diagrams
solution: 7 clear steps with correct modules enabling sub-flow drill-down; added 3 diagrams to ideal/ptt.md: main flow, tool loop, interrupt path

problem: Add tray_controller step to config.yaml; add architecture diagram to ideal/app_startup.md
root_cause: config.yaml missing tray_controller step 8; no architecture diagram
solution: Added tray_controller as final step; added startup sequence diagram with health-check branch

problem: Fix first_run steps: wrong welcome order, missing FIRST_RUN_COMPLETED write, missing mode_management, tutorial_integration should be separate
root_cause: welcome order wrong (after permissions), missing FIRST_RUN_COMPLETED write step and mode_management, tutorial_integration was embedded
solution: Fixed 6 steps with correct order: check→welcome→permissions→write flag→post-welcome→SLEEPING; added flow diagram with skip branch

problem: Tutorial steps missing PTT wait, user practice run, TUTORIAL_VERSION write; need architecture diagram
root_cause: Tutorial had 3 steps missing PTT wait, practice run, TUTORIAL_VERSION write; bool flag instead of version string
solution: 6 steps with PTT timeout, practice run, version write; tutorial.md updated with TUTORIAL_VERSION concept + architecture diagram

problem: Missing speech_playback stop step and grpc_client open step; wrong module name state_manager vs mode_management
root_cause: Missing speech_playback (stop audio) and grpc_client (open stream) steps; state_manager named incorrectly
solution: 5 steps: detect PTT → stop audio → LISTENING → open stream → mic on; added diagram

problem: Missing volume save and restore steps; wrong trigger (PTT instead of MODE_CHANGED→SPEAKING); volume stays at 20% permanently if not restored
root_cause: Missing volume save/restore steps; wrong trigger; volume stayed at 20% permanently
solution: 6 steps: duck on SPEAKING (save+set 20%), restore on PLAYBACK_COMPLETE (restore+fallback 100%); added diagram

problem: Add scenario sub-flows to email flow with LLM-level steps and status indicators
root_cause: Email had 5 generic module steps; no scenario sub-flows from SKILL.md
solution: 12 scenarios from SKILL.md: read/find/send/reply/edge cases with correct tool chains including email_reply_to_last and tag=verification

problem: Tool call errors not visible in map — when email_read_all returns status:error, map shows green instead of red
root_cause: Tool call errors (status:error) were not reported to runtime_errors.json, so Flow steps stayed green even when tools failed
solution: Added error reporting in both sync and async tool result handling paths in orchestrator.py using getLogger(server.tools.<tool_name>) so map module_id matches flow step module

problem: E-SR-002: empty/short transcript passed silently to LLM instead of speaking I did not catch that
root_cause: E-SR-002: empty transcript passed silently to LLM; user heard nothing when Whisper returned empty result
solution: In processing_workflow._on_recognition_failed: when error==empty_result, publish grpc.tts_request I did not catch that before setting recognition_failed; workflow waits for playback.completed to complete chain -> SLEEPING

problem: E-SYS-002/E-MOD-004: no watchdog — stuck non-SLEEPING states require app restart
root_cause: Gap was already closed before this session
solution: Watchdog fully implemented in mode_management_integration._watchdog_guard(): 30s asyncio timer, publishes mode.request SLEEPING on timeout. Marked fixed in ideal docs.

problem: E-AI-002/E-AI-004: Claude API failure and loop limit → silent SLEEPING, no spoken phrase
root_cause: E-AI-002: API exception yielded error event directly; grpc_server returned raw exception string silently. E-AI-004 was already fixed in orchestrator.py
solution: Added text event with Server error phrase BEFORE error event in _run_orchestrator, so text_chunk reaches client TTS before stream terminates

problem: TUTORIAL_COMPLETED bool cannot detect new features — replace with LAST_TUTORIAL_VERSION from VERSION file
root_cause: Gap was wrong — tutorial already uses ledger with per-pack version tracking, not a single bool
solution: System already works: new delta pack in config.yaml → reconcile adds it as pending → selector finds it → shown automatically. Updated ideal docs.

problem: code field missing in tool results — server cannot distinguish error types
root_cause: dispatch wrapper only caught success:False but not status:error; email reply/send missing specific codes
solution: 3 fixes: (1) wrapper now catches status==error too; (2) email_reply_to_last gets E-EMAIL-005; (3) send_email failure gets E-EMAIL-003 via setdefault

problem: E-GRPC-003: reconnect has no retry limit — can loop indefinitely on connection loss
root_cause: Gap was wrong — _ensure_connected_in_grpc_loop already has max_retries=3 with exp backoff since initial implementation
solution: Updated ideal docs to mark E-GRPC-001 and E-GRPC-003 as fixed

problem: E-PERM-002/003: Accessibility/Screen denied can crash instead of degraded mode
root_cause: Gap description was inaccurate. V2 orchestrator with default config (require_all_hard_pass=true) returns should_restart=false when accessibility/screen is denied, falls through to _complete(full_mode=True), publishes system.ready_to_greet correctly.
solution: No code fix needed. App already launches in degraded mode when hard permissions are denied. On-demand NSAlert added separately (v5.0.0.190) to inform user when they trigger a denied-permission feature.

problem: Online monitoring dashboard: cloud_push.py + map.html dual mode + GitHub Pages on nexy-monitor repo
root_cause: Not a code gap — infrastructure already configured
solution: cloud_push.py running, GitHub Pages live at seregawpn.github.io/nexy-monitor/. Dual-mode already in map.html (IS_STATIC flag).

problem: E-GRPC-004: missing audio chunks not detected — partial response played as complete
root_cause: Gap was theoretical — AudioChunk proto has no seq_num field; TCP/gRPC guarantees ordered delivery; missing chunk = stream failure not silent partial
solution: Docs updated to mark as not applicable

problem: Real-time monitoring: replace poll watcher with watchdog + add asyncio exception handler in server/client
root_cause: poll watcher (10s interval)
solution: Replaced FileWatcher with watchdog.Observer in watcher.py. Instant FSEvents notification, 1s debounce, mtime filter against FSEvents replay.

problem: file_search directory scope: LLM sets directory without enforcement, no broaden-on-irrelevant-results fallback (F4f leads CSV on Desktop not found, search scoped to documents)
root_cause: file_search default scope was effectively single-folder: LLM often passed directory="documents" (or other folder) even when the user did not name a folder, and _DIRECTORY_KEYWORDS["documents"]=("document",) matched the generic word "document" in queries like "find my bank statements document", so Guard #1 never stripped it. With no broaden-on-empty retry and file_searcher requiring an exact folder match when directory was set, results were silently confined to one folder.
solution: Guard #1 (before_tool_call) now strips directory from file_search unless the user actually named that folder via _DIRECTORY_KEYWORDS; documents now requires explicit phrases ("documents folder","my documents","in documents","in the documents") so the bare word "document" no longer matches. Guard #2 (on_turn_end) forces one retry without directory if a scoped search returns 0 candidates. file_searcher.search() defaults to {desktop,downloads,documents} when directory is omitted (Messages/Mail still require explicit directory). Verified via 35/35 unit tests in test_hook_continuation_guard.py + new tests in test_file_searcher.py, and F4f/F4g E2E re-runs showing broadened result sets including Desktop. problem: Installed app restart loop every 18-24s: auto_restart=true causes instance_manager to SIGKILL the launchd-managed instance, which launchd immediately respawns
root_cause: launchd-managed application.com.nexy.assistant.* job auto-respawns its PID on exit ("because launch job demand"); instance_manager.auto_restart=true caused a second LaunchServices-spawned instance to detect the launchd-managed one as a duplicate and SIGKILL it after a 4s grace period, which launchd immediately respawned, repeating every 18-40s

problem: EmailInboxWatcherIntegration scans Mail.app at every app startup (unconditional), triggering Mail Automation TCC prompt simultaneously with first-run permission wizard dialogs
root_cause: EmailInboxWatcherIntegration._do_start() unconditionally called _start_mail_store(), which spawns daemon threads making AppleScript calls to Mail.app at app startup, concurrently with the sequential first-run permission wizard — causing the Mail Automation TCC prompt to appear together with all other permission prompts instead of on-demand.
solution: _do_start() now subscribes to tool.submit_pending (LOW priority) instead of calling _start_mail_store() directly. New _on_tool_submit_pending(event) starts _start_mail_store() only on the first dispatched command in EMAIL_ACTION_COMMANDS (12 commands owned by EmailInboxWatcherIntegration, via get_action_commands_by_owner). _do_stop() unsubscribes. Mail Automation prompt now appears only on first voice-driven email request.

problem: Audible click on AirPods caused by AVAudioSession category switch (A2DP<->HFP) on every PTT press/release
root_cause: On AirPods, every voice_recording_start/voice_mic_closed switches AVAudioSessionCategoryPlayback (AllowBluetoothA2DP) <-> AVAudioSessionCategoryPlayAndRecord (no AllowBluetoothA2DP), forcing an A2DP<->HFP profile renegotiation on the headset; if audio is actively playing at that instant (or player_node.stop() cuts mid-buffer on interrupt), the renegotiation/stop is audible as a click. Confirmed applied=true on 28/28 AirPods PTT cycles in nexy-dev.log.
solution: avf_player.py: new _mute_for_transition()/_restore_player_volume(); _apply_audio_session_profile() mutes player_node before setCategory and restores volume after; stop_playback(force_stop_node=True) mutes before player_node.stop(). Released as v5.0.0.348.

problem: E-MOD-004 watchdog forces SLEEPING during active playback (bypasses sleep-guard blocker check); also one-shot watchdog wont retry if deferred
root_cause: E-MOD-004 watchdog forced mode.request{target=SLEEPING, source=watchdog_E-MOD-004} went straight to _apply_mode, bypassing the sleep-guard blocker check (_collect_blockers_for_sleep_guard) that ProcessingWorkflow.processing_*/processing.unblock.* sources already pass through, so the app mode flipped to SLEEPING while TTS playback/browser/actions were still active. Additionally the watchdog is one-shot and only re-arms on app.mode_changed.
solution: _on_mode_request guard at mode_management_integration.py:622-651 now also matches source==watchdog_E-MOD-004: if blockers are active, defer via _deferred_sleep_sessions (finalized later by _try_finalize_sleep) and re-arm the watchdog via _reset_watchdog(current_mode); if no blockers, apply SLEEPING immediately as before. Added test_mode_request_sleeping_from_watchdog_e_mod_004_deferred_by_active_playback. Updated mode_tray.md, CONTRACT_CATALOG.md, KNOWN_ISSUES.md (Gap D/E follow-ups), CHANGELOG.md, INDEX.md. v5.0.0.402.

solution: Added grpc.request_inflight event published from grpc_client_integration._inflight mutations (4 sites: _maybe_send dispatch, _delayed_send completion, _on_recording_stop stale reset, _on_request_cancel), consumed by mode_management_integration._on_grpc_request_inflight -> _active_request_sessions -> new request_inflight sleep-guard blocker. root_cause: TASK COMPLETION DISCIPLINE (browser_llm.py:747-763) required exact counts for repeatable actions but never defined a default for a count-less scroll, nor bounded open-ended 'to the end' requests; ScrollAction.pages (browser_use/tools/views.py:79-82) was the unused real lever for scroll amount.
solution: Extended TASK COMPLETION DISCIPLINE with a SCROLL AMOUNT sub-rule: no count -> one call pages=1.0; explicit count N -> one call pages=N; 'to the end/bottom/top' -> one bounded call pages~=10, using the library's own parameter instead of chaining repeated scroll calls.

problem: FACTUAL ANSWER GROUNDING forces an extra extraction round even for simple existence/yes-no questions, and when it does, the final answer names irrelevant surrounding items instead of the ones actually asked about
root_cause: FACTUAL ANSWER GROUNDING forced an extra extract_enforcement_retry round for every final answer regardless of question type, and had no rule tying named specific items back to the actual subject asked about — live repro: a yes/no Shorts-existence question already had a correct concise answer at step 2, but the forced extra round produced a final answer naming unrelated surrounding videos instead of the real Shorts titles already seen in step 1.
solution: Added EXISTENCE/YES-NO QUESTIONS rule (extract as usual, state the direct yes/no fact, then stop -- no further elaboration once confirmed) and WHEN NAMING SPECIFIC ITEMS rule (named items must be the ones actually asked about, not positional landmarks) to FACTUAL ANSWER GROUNDING in browser_llm.py. Extract remains mandatory for every task; only the post-confirmation stopping point is bounded. Verified the existing regression guard ('extract is not required' not in message) still passes, 11/11 tests green.

problem: Downloaded Chrome for Testing binary lacks NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription in its Info.plist, so macOS SIGKILLs the browser process (TCC privacy enforcement) whenever it touches a Bluetooth-gated API, killing an in-progress browser_use task
root_cause: Playwright's downloaded 'Google Chrome for Testing' bundle ships without NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription in its Info.plist; macOS TCC SIGKILLs any process touching a Bluetooth-gated API without that key declared, confirmed via an actual macOS crash report (EXC_CRASH/SIGKILL, namespace=TCC) captured mid browser_use-task.
solution: Added _patch_chromium_privacy_usage_descriptions() to browser_runtime_install.py, adding the missing key via plistlib (no subprocess) right after the executable is confirmed present -- on both the fresh-install path and the already-installed fast path, so existing caches get patched too. Confirmed safe: the bundle's ad-hoc code signature does not seal Info.plist. 4 new tests cover missing-key, already-present, non-macOS no-op, and missing-bundle no-op cases.

problem: FACTUAL ANSWER GROUNDING list-item rule requires naming SOME specific items but not how many, so the agent can name a small arbitrary handful even when many more similar items are visible, under-reporting page content and causing follow-up answers to just repeat the same few items
root_cause: v5.0.0.824's list-item rule required naming SOME specific items but never specified how many, so a technically-compliant answer could name a small arbitrary handful while under-reporting most of what was actually visible/extracted; live repro showed the same unchanged page yielding 4 items on the first answer and ~25 on a follow-up.
solution: Added LIST COVERAGE (name all items visible without scrolling, or a representative set spanning the full range plus 'and several others' if too many) and a follow-up rule (add genuinely new items/detail on repeat requests about the same page, don't restate the previous answer) to FACTUAL ANSWER GROUNDING in browser_llm.py. 2 new tests, 13/13 passing.

problem: browser_use agent system prompt lacks hard rule against clicking/interacting on read-only describe tasks, allowing accidental media playback
root_cause: _build_agent_system_message() only advised trying extract first for read-only tasks (FACTUAL ANSWER GROUNDING), never hard-forbidding click/type/submit/play/navigate, so the browser-use agent could still interact with the page (e.g. click a video thumbnail) on a plain read/describe request, sometimes starting media playback.
solution: Added a READ-ONLY TASK RESTRICTION section to _build_agent_system_message() in client/modules/browser_automation/browser_llm.py: for tasks that only ask to read/check/find out/describe, the agent must not click/type/submit/play/pause/navigate — only scroll and extract are allowed.

problem: browser_use switch-to-existing-tab request repeatedly lands on an empty/unresponsive YouTube tab despite verified internet connectivity
root_cause: v5.0.0.847 dropped target_tab/tab_intent/tab_reason from the browser_use LLM contract assuming they were unused; browser_request_orchestration.py's _resolve_request_target_tab() still defaults to current when absent, which both instructs the agent to stay on the current tab and keeps _enforce_owned_content_tab()'s step-callback guard active, forcibly refocusing back to the original tab after every step -- confirmed by user as a regression, working before v5.0.0.847.
solution: Restored target_tab (current|existing|new) to the browser_use SKILL.md contract -- existing for Switch to a tab, new for Open a new blank tab, omitted elsewhere; updated test_browser_skill_prompt.py to match.

problem: Active-browser followup guard (_force_browser_followup_action) is defined but never invoked in either run() or arun_streaming(), so action:null answers while a browser session is active fall through to a generic canned reply instead of re-invoking browser_use
root_cause: _force_browser_followup_action() was added in v5.0.0.845/846 to convert an action:null answer into a fresh browser_use call while a browser session is active, but was never actually called anywhere -- not in run() (which computes browser_followup_task but never applies it) and not in arun_streaming() (the real production path), which also never computed browser_followup_task at all. Live repro: with Amazon open, 'Go to best seller' fell through to the generic canned reply 'I'm here. How can I help?' instead of navigating.
solution: Added browser_followup_task computation + _force_browser_followup_action() call on iteration 1 to both run() and arun_streaming(); in arun_streaming(), also suppress live sentence-streaming of the action:null text whenever the force is about to override it, since the streaming loop yields sentences token-by-token before the full response is parsed -- without suppression the wrong text would already be spoken before the override took effect.

problem: Follow-up action requests (e.g. "click it", "open it") referencing an item already named in a prior browser_use answer are routed as bare context-free tasks, causing a fresh agent with no memory of prior turns to misinterpret the target (e.g. searching Amazon instead of clicking a homepage section a
root_cause: Live repro: 'click on Premium summer picks section' (a context-free follow-up task) reached a fresh browser-use agent with no memory of the prior turn that had already found this section on the Amazon homepage. The agent's system prompt had no instruction to check the current page before treating a named section as a search query, so it typed the name into Amazon's search bar and searched the whole site instead of scrolling the current page, eventually reporting the section as unavailable even though it was visible seconds earlier.
solution: Added a CHECK THE CURRENT PAGE BEFORE SEARCHING ELSEWHERE section to _build_agent_system_message() (client/modules/browser_automation/browser_llm.py) -- before using site search or navigating away, the agent must first scroll the current page to check if the named item/section is already visible there. Fixed in the browser agent's own prompt, not the server-side SKILL.md routing prompt (user correction: the routing task was fine, the failure was the agent not checking the current page).
